title: construction fails when a field is still unbound after the constructor
purpose: The completeness check runs after the constructor, on the path actually taken.

failure.justification: The owner rule checks completeness after the constructor has run, so Gate(true) is a valid construction and only Gate(false) fails, when it is executed.

provenance.origin: authored for OCS 0.1.0 from the cited contract text
provenance.expected_basis: language owner decision, 19.10.2026 (D-035, refined): before the constructor runs, every defaulted field is filled with its default; the constructor then binds the supplied values, replacing defaults; finally every field must be bound, otherwise construction fails. Gate(true) binds a and succeeds; Gate(false) leaves a unbound, so construction dies at runtime.
